handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught and framework-caught errors reach PostHog from both browser and Next.js server runtimes, using the SDK/framework-supported global mechanisms rather than scattered manual handlers.
handoff.did: Added `app/global-error.tsx` as the App Router global error boundary; it reports errors swallowed by Next.js through `posthog.captureException(error)` and provides a retry action. Added root `instrumentation.ts` with Next.js `onRequestError`; for Node.js requests it obtains the shared server client, recovers the PostHog distinct ID from the analytics cookie when available, captures the exception, and awaits `flush()` for request-lifecycle delivery. Updated `libs/posthog-ai.ts` to expose its existing singleton server client and enable Node SDK exception autocapture, with `flushAt: 1` and `flushInterval: 0`; existing AI capture continues to use the same client. Browser global unhandled exceptions remain covered by the pre-existing `capture_exceptions: true` in `instrumentation-client.ts`. These mechanisms feed PostHog Error Tracking exception views and preserve linkage to the browser person where a PostHog cookie is available.
handoff.forNextAgent: Error tracking is now covered once per runtime: browser SDK exception autocapture plus the Next.js global boundary, and Node SDK exception autocapture plus `onRequestError`. `posthog-node` was already declared in the root manifest, so nothing was installed. The app has no Edge-specific PostHog server capture; the hook intentionally gates on `NEXT_RUNTIME === "nodejs"` because `posthog-node` is the documented Node runtime path.
handoff.evidence: Ran `pnpm build`. Next.js 16.4.3 compiled successfully, completed TypeScript checking, collected page data, and generated all static pages successfully.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed deployed server-side Next.js execution uses the Node.js runtime, consistent with the existing `posthog-node` integration and `next start` script. No explicit Edge runtime files were present in the scoped entry-point inspection.
